cipher_bundle.name: ReverseAlphabetCipher

description_json.name: Reverse Alphabet Cipher
description_json.idea: To minimize cognitive load and reasoning errors for the model, this cipher uses a classic Atbash-style reverse alphabet mapping. Each letter is replaced by its mirror image in the alphabet (A becomes Z, B becomes Y, etc.). Case is preserved. Numbers, spaces, and punctuation remain completely unchanged. This is a highly intuitive, single-step bijection that reduces noise and maintains structural coherence.
description_json.encrypt_rules:
For any English letter, map its position from the start of the alphabet to the same position from the end of the alphabet. Specifically:
- Uppercase: 'A' <-> 'Z', 'B' <-> 'Y', 'C' <-> 'X', 'D' <-> 'W', 'E' <-> 'V', 'F' <-> 'U', 'G' <-> 'T', 'H' <-> 'S', 'I' <-> 'R', 'J' <-> 'Q', 'K' <-> 'P', 'L' <-> 'O', 'M' <-> 'N'
- Lowercase: 'a' <-> 'z', 'b' <-> 'y', 'c' <-> 'x', 'd' <-> 'w', 'e' <-> 'v', 'f' <-> 'u', 'g' <-> 't', 'h' <-> 's', 'i' <-> 'r', 'j' <-> 'q', 'k' <-> 'p', 'l' <-> 'o', 'm' <-> 'n'
- All non-alphabetic characters (digits, spaces, punctuation) remain unchanged.
description_json.decrypt_rules: Since the mapping is its own inverse, the decryption rules are identical to the encryption rules. Apply the same mirror mapping to revert the ciphertext back to plaintext.

description_json.name: QWERTY monoalphabetic substitution cipher
description_json.idea: A fixed one-to-one substitution over the English alphabet. Each plaintext letter is replaced by exactly one ciphertext letter using a single bijection, and the mapping is the same for uppercase and lowercase letters. Non-letter characters are left unchanged.
description_json.encrypt_rules: Use the following bijection: plaintext alphabet abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz -> ciphertext alphabet qwertyuiopasdfghjklzxcvbnm. Thus a->q, b->w, c->e, d->r, e->t, f->y, g->u, h->i, i->o, j->p, k->a, l->s, m->d, n->f, o->g, p->h, q->j, r->k, s->l, t->z, u->x, v->c, w->v, x->b, y->n, z->m. Uppercase letters use the same mapping, preserving case. All non-letter characters remain unchanged.
description_json.decrypt_rules: Use the inverse bijection: ciphertext alphabet qwertyuiopasdfghjklzxcvbnm -> plaintext alphabet abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz. Thus q->a, w->b, e->c, r->d, t->e, y->f, u->g, i->h, o->i, p->j, a->k, s->l, d->m, f->n, g->o, h->p, j->q, k->r, l->s, z->t, x->u, c->v, v->w, b->x, n->y, m->z. Uppercase letters use the same mapping, preserving case. All non-letter characters remain unchanged.

ciphers.name: VowelConsonantAlternatingShift

description_json.name: Vowel-Consonant Alternating Shift
description_json.idea: To maintain high semantic readability and reduce model reasoning errors, this cipher applies a very simple, low-noise rule: vowels are shifted forward by 1 position in the vowel sequence (a->e, e->i, i->o, o->u, u->a), while consonants are shifted forward by 1 position in the alphabet, skipping vowels. Case is preserved. Numbers, spaces, and punctuation remain completely unchanged.
description_json.encrypt_rules:
1. Identify if the character is a letter. If not, keep it unchanged.
2. If it is a vowel (a, e, i, o, u - case insensitive):
   - Shift to the next vowel in the cycle: a -> e, e -> i, i -> o, o -> u, u -> a (preserve uppercase: A -> E, etc.).
3. If it is a consonant:
   - Shift to the next consonant in the alphabet (b->c, c->d, d->f, f->g, g->h, h->j, j->k, k->l, l->m, m->n, n->p, p->q, q->r, r->s, s->t, t->v, v->w, w->x, x->y, y->z, z->b). Preserve uppercase.
description_json.decrypt_rules:
1. Identify if the character is a letter. If not, keep it unchanged.
2. If it is a vowel (a, e, i, o, u - case insensitive):
   - Shift to the previous vowel in the cycle: a -> u, e -> a, i -> e, o -> i, u -> o (preserve uppercase: A -> U, etc.).
3. If it is a consonant:
   - Shift to the previous consonant in the alphabet (b->z, c->b, d->c, f->d, g->f, h->g, j->h, k->j, l->k, m->l, n->m, p->n, q->p, r->q, s->r, t->s, v->t, w->v, x->w, y->x, z->y). Preserve uppercase.
